name: Russia–NATO
summary: Russian nuclear warnings over Kaliningrad stand; no Article 4 request as of 5 Nov
state: Russia warned NATO in late September, including in a formal diplomatic note, that it would use 'all means', including nuclear weapons, against any action on Kaliningrad; NATO's Mark Rutte called the threats unhelpful (Arms Control Association, Nov issue). Russia's mass strike on Ukraine on 3–4 Nov hit Kovel in Volyn, near the Polish border (The Defense Post). No NATO member had requested Article 4 consultations as of 5 Nov.
for_you: Travellers to eastern NATO states should follow FCDO travel advice. Airspace closures near the Ukrainian border can disrupt flights at short notice.
rubric_hit: Explicit threats against members; no Article 4 or clash = Watch

sources.title: Arms Control Association — Russia issues nuclear threats over Kaliningrad
The Defense Post — Russia fires 310 drones at Ukraine day after mass strike on energy grid

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
